result.summary:
REGISTRY LOOKUP (Step 0.5): grep of docs/issues/ for role-credit|persona.actor|candidate.group hit ISS-0739 (resolved; the swiftroute equivalent: TASK_WORKER-only actors + missing role-ops-manager/role-ceo groups, fixed by scripts/seed_swiftroute_persona_actors.sh per lib/letflow/design/iss-0761-swiftroute-persona-actor-provisioning.md) and ISS-0931 itself. NOT a recurrence: same CLASS of defect for two tenants ISS-0739 never covered (it was scoped to swiftroute only). Note ISS-0739/0761 left the same gap open for any non-swiftroute tenant; this issue is its direct follow-on. Local filename ISS-0931 (queue ref Q-914 collides with an existing ISS-0914.yaml; unrelated).

ROOT CAUSE (data/seed gap, NOT a lib/ defect): the meridian and vortex process definitions published by scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh and scripts/seed_vortex_definition.sh contain HUMAN_TASK nodes routed by a `role` attribute naming process-routing roles (role-*). The task engine stores these as assignee_type ROLE / assignee_ref <role-name>. Nothing provisions the matching tenant_roles rows (kind process_routing_role, bound to a group) nor any group memberships in the meridian or vortex tenants; no scripts/seed_meridian_persona_actors.sh or seed_vortex_persona_actors.sh exists (scripts/ has only seed_meridian_definition.sh, seed_swiftroute_definition.sh, seed_swiftroute_persona_actors.sh, seed_vortex_definition.sh, seed_vortex_entities.sh; seed_vortex_entities.sh only creates entity grants for anna/karl and does not touch groups/roles). QA state observed by UAT-RUNNER (test/uat-reports/uat-2026-10-01-ISS0912-NARRATIVE.yaml observed_facts, finding D2 at lines 189-192): GET /identity/roles and /groups in both tenants list only the six platform roles; inbox count 0; claim -> 409 'caller does not hold the assigned role'.

MECHANISM (verified from code): (1) Letflow.Tasks.resolve_principal_scope/2 (lib/letflow/tasks.ex:338-358) computes role_names = names of TenantRole rows whose group_id is in the caller's group memberships (GroupMember). A tenant with no process_routing_role rows, or with the actor in no such group, yields role_names without the process role. (2) Inbox/list: filter_by_assignee_scope (lib/letflow/tasks.ex:~660-671) matches `assignee_type == "ROLE" and assignee_ref in role_names` so the ROLE task is invisible -> empty inbox. (3) Claim: apply_claim ROLE clause (lib/letflow/tasks.ex:462-476) returns {:error, :assignee_role_not_held} unless ref in scope.role_names; lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex:406 maps that to Response.conflict 'caller does not hold the assigned role' (409). Nothing in the engine requires the group to exist as a name match; ONLY the tenant_roles(name)->group_id->group_members chain. LOCAL REPRODUCTION: MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/routers/tasks_test.exs:1798 --seed 0 -> 'Result: 1 passed, 60 excluded'. That test ('the same role-assigned task is REJECTED when claimed by a non-member (ISS-0905)', tasks_test.exs:1798-1821) creates a ROLE task (assignee_ref approver), a user in an unrelated group/role, and asserts claim -> 409 with the task row unchanged (assignee_type ROLE) -- exactly the QA symptom; a user not bound through tenant_roles to ref gets 409. The 'no such group at all' case is a strict subset (role_names has no entry). I did NOT run anything against QA and did NOT run any seed script.

WHY NOT CAUGHT: seed definitions were authored by ISS-0897 (meridian/vortex definition seeding) which published definitions only; persona/role provisioning was only designed for swiftroute (ISS-0761 design section 1 scope) and no UAT precondition check verified role groups exist before the scenarios ran (the preflight report test/uat-reports/preflight-2026-09-30-qa.txt predates this).

ROLE-* GROUPS REFERENCED (source = payloads actually published by the seeds; test/fixtures/qa/*.json, via scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh:161,167 and scripts/seed_vortex_definition.sh:164,170; same literals in test/fixtures/simulation/{meridian,vortex}/process_*.yaml):
MERIDIAN (tenant meridian):
- Loan Origination (meridian_loan_origination_process_definition.json): credit-memo-review L19 role-credit-manager; risk-assessment L35 role-risk-manager; kyc-manual-review L60 role-compliance-officer; l1-approval L92 role-credit-manager; l2-approval L99 role-credit-director; credit-committee-vote L106 role-committee-member; disburse-loan L131 role-loan-ops.
- Regulatory Compliance Review (meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json): evidence-collection L15 role-compliance-officer; risk-evaluation L31 role-risk-manager; findings-sign-off L68 role-cro; ceo-override L84 role-ceo.
Distinct meridian set (8): role-credit-manager, role-risk-manager, role-compliance-officer, role-credit-director, role-committee-member, role-loan-ops, role-cro, role-ceo.
VORTEX (tenant vortex):
- Production Order Release (vortex_production_order_release_process_definition.json): capacity-review L15 role-production-manager; escalate-to-ceo L22 role-ceo; budget-approval L33 role-controller.
- Supplier Quality Deviation (vortex_supplier_quality_deviation_process_definition.json): severity-classification L24 role-quality-manager.
Distinct vortex set (4): role-production-manager, role-controller, role-quality-manager, role-ceo.
DISCREPANCY: the UAT narrative lists role-procurement-manager as missing, but NO published vortex definition references it (it only appears in the scenario prose test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/vortex/supplier-quality-deviation-critical.yaml:108-114). Do not seed it unless CODE-DESIGNER decides the scenario requires it (recommend: do not; flag as scenario/definition mismatch for BA-VORTEX, out of scope).

PERSONAS (usernames per scenario actors: blocks, test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/{meridian,vortex}/*.yaml; people per test/fixtures/simulation/{meridian,vortex}/org_structure.yaml; Keycloak accounts for these actors already exist on QA per the narrative, which logged in as them) and PROPOSED MAPPING (every actor TASK_WORKER for API access, as in the swiftroute design section 4; plus role group):
MERIDIAN: actor-meridian-ben -> role-credit-manager; actor-meridian-miriam -> role-risk-manager; actor-meridian-claudia -> role-compliance-officer; actor-meridian-julia -> role-credit-director + role-committee-member (scenario committee_member_director); actor-meridian-thomas -> role-committee-member + role-cro (scenario committee_member_cro; org structure dept-risk); actor-meridian-eva -> role-committee-member + role-ceo (committee_member_ceo, ceo); actor-meridian-marcus -> role-loan-ops; actor-meridian-lars, -sophie (analysts) -> TASK_WORKER only; actor-meridian-oliver (dept-risk, unused by any scenario) -> TASK_WORKER only (or role-risk-manager; designer's call, recommend TASK_WORKER only).
VORTEX: actor-vortex-sabine -> role-production-manager; actor-vortex-stefan -> role-controller; actor-vortex-karl -> role-quality-manager; actor-vortex-dirk -> role-ceo (dept-exec; not a scenario actor, needed for escalate-to-ceo); actor-vortex-anna (planner), -nina (quality engineer), -felix (procurement), -max, -claudia -> TASK_WORKER only. NOTE: the actor roster is partly inferred (e.g. thomas->role-cro, dirk->role-ceo are derived from org_structure/dept, not stated verbatim in a scenario actor map); CODE-DESIGNER should state this assumption and cite org_structure.yaml.

THE FIX MUST ADD (mirror scripts/seed_swiftroute_persona_actors.sh, which the design lib/letflow/design/iss-0761-swiftroute-persona-actor-provisioning.md specifies): (1) scripts/seed_meridian_persona_actors.sh and (2) scripts/seed_vortex_persona_actors.sh, each: require QA_AUTH_TOKEN (PLATFORM_ADMIN of that tenant with GroupsManage+RolesManage+UsersManage) and QA_URL; resolve TASK_WORKER group id from GET /identity/roles; for each role-* above: idempotent ensure_group (GET /identity/groups, POST if absent) then upsert_role via POST /identity/roles {name, kind: process_routing_role, group_id} (upsert); lookup_user_id per actor via GET /identity/users?search=<actor> aborting cleanly if Part A (Keycloak/JIT sync) is missing; add_group_member (200/201 idempotent) per mapping. Prefer factoring the shared helpers (lookup_user_id, find_group_id, ensure_group, upsert_role, add_group_member) into scripts/lib/ (a seed_service_task_base.sh already exists there as precedent) rather than copy-pasting three times; do not modify the swiftroute script's behavior. (3) A bash/unit-level test is feasible without QA: the existing script test pattern (check test/ for scripts tests and ISS-0761's test spec) with a stubbed curl; verify idempotency and the mapping tables, and that the role-name sets equal the role literals extracted from the four test/fixtures/qa/*process_definition.json (a drift guard that fails if a definition adds a role the seed omits -- this is the fail-first/regression test: pre-fix the script files do not exist, and per WF-03 'non-existence' rule TEST-DESIGNER must also mutate the mapping, e.g. drop a role or a membership, and show the guard fails). (4) Update .claude/agents/uat-runner.md / docs uat docs and the preflight check to list the new scripts as a precondition for meridian/vortex scenarios (mirrors ISS-0761 section 5). (5) No change needed to scripts/seed_*_definition.sh or the definitions. EXECUTION against QA is a separate post-merge ops step (needs tenant admin tokens via ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-uat-env.sh); the pipeline should not claim the QA symptom is cleared until UAT-RUNNER re-runs the 7 scenarios (note D1 BLOCKER, ISS-0930 service-task endpoints, and D3 are independent and may still fail those scenarios).

lib/ / AUTHZ SCOPE: NO lib/ or migration change; no tenant-data path, API route, response shape or secret touched. The scripts only call existing identity endpoints (POST /groups, POST /roles, POST /groups/:id/members) as a tenant PLATFORM_ADMIN. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate is likely not triggered; REVIEWER still applies. Related but SEPARATE (do not fold in): UAT finding D5 (POST /tasks/:id/complete does not enforce ROLE membership while claim does; narrative observed 200 completes by non-holders) is a potential security-adjacent authz gap in lib/letflow/tasks.ex / routers/tasks.ex and must be triaged as its own issue by ORCH/SECURITY-REVIEWER -- seeding groups does not address it (arguably makes it less visible). Also separate: D4 (complete on an ERROR instance returns 500).
